mcqs.q: OPG stands for:
mcqs.explain: OPG = OrthoPantomoGram (pantomography); 'panoramic' means an unobstructed view in every direction.

mcqs.q: A panoramic radiograph produces:
opts: A single tomographic image of both the maxillary and mandibular arches
An axial slice of the skull base
mcqs.explain: OPG gives one tomographic image of both jaws and their supporting structures.

mcqs.q: Tomography works by:
opts: Keeping one layer in focus while blurring structures in other planes
mcqs.explain: Tomography images one section/layer in focus and blurs out the structures in other planes.

mcqs.q: Which is a recognised indication for a panoramic radiograph?
opts: Assessment of impacted teeth, cysts/tumours and TMJ disorders
mcqs.explain: OPG suits large-coverage tasks: impacted teeth, cysts/tumours, fractures, mixed-dentition analysis, periodontal bone levels, implants and TMJ disorders.

mcqs.q: A key ADVANTAGE of panoramic radiography is:
opts: Coverage of the entire dentition on a single film, quickly and comfortably
Excellent for detecting small interproximal caries
mcqs.explain: OPG covers the whole dentition on one film, is easy, quick and well accepted — but detail/sharpness are limited.

mcqs.q: Which is a DISADVANTAGE of panoramic radiography?
opts: Magnification, distortion, overlapping and ghost shadows
mcqs.explain: OPG suffers from inadequate sharpness, magnification, geometric distortion, overlapping, and soft-tissue/ghost shadows.

mcqs.q: The main components of a panoramic unit are the:
opts: X-ray tube head, head positioner and exposure controls
mcqs.explain: A panoramic machine consists of the x-ray tube head, a head positioner, and exposure controls.

mcqs.q: On a panoramic machine, which exposure factor CANNOT be changed?
mcqs.explain: kVp and mA are adjustable (typically 60–80 kVp), but the exposure time is fixed by the rotation cycle.

mcqs.q: During panoramic radiography a lead apron is used, but a thyroid collar is OMITTED because:
opts: It would block part of the rotating x-ray beam
mcqs.explain: A thyroid collar is not used in OPG because it would block part of the beam as the tube rotates around the neck.

mcqs.q: Correct panoramic head positioning requires the:
opts: Mid-sagittal plane perpendicular to the floor and Frankfurt plane parallel to it
Mid-sagittal plane parallel to the floor
Frankfurt plane perpendicular to the floor
mcqs.explain: The mid-sagittal plane is set perpendicular to the floor and the Frankfurt plane roughly parallel to it, with the incisors edge-to-edge in the bite block.

mcqs.q: The patient bites so that the central incisors are:
opts: Edge-to-edge in the groove of a bite block
mcqs.explain: The maxillary and mandibular central incisors are placed edge-to-edge in the bite-block groove to centre them in the focal trough.

mcqs.q: The basic principle of panoramic imaging uses two rotating disks where:
opts: The x-ray tube and the receptor move in OPPOSITE directions
The tube and receptor move in the same direction
mcqs.explain: Disk 1 (tube) and Disk 2 (receptor) rotate in opposite directions; the synchronized movement keeps a narrow focal trough in sharp focus.

mcqs.q: Lead SLIT collimators at the source and receptor serve to:
opts: Limit the beam to a narrow slit, defining the sharp image layer
mcqs.explain: Slit-shaped lead collimators restrict the central ray to a narrow beam, which together with the synchronized motion produces the focal trough.

mcqs.q: During the exposure, the centre of rotation:
opts: Continuously moves, because the dental arches are curved
mcqs.explain: Because the arches are curved, the machine shifts the rotation centre continuously (a continuously moving rotation centre) during the cycle.

mcqs.q: The focal trough (image layer) is best described as:
opts: A 3-D horseshoe-shaped zone in which structures are reasonably sharp
A flat 2-D plane through the midline
A single point at the centre
mcqs.explain: The focal trough is a three-dimensional curved (horseshoe) zone, shaped like the dental arches, in which structures are in reasonable focus.

mcqs.q: The three dimensions of the focal trough are:
mcqs.explain: The focal trough has antero-posterior (front-to-back), bucco-lingual (side-to-side) and vertical (up-down) dimensions.

mcqs.q: How does the position of the rotation centre affect the focal trough?
opts: The closer it is to the teeth, the narrower the focal trough there
The closer it is, the wider the trough
mcqs.explain: The nearer the rotation centre lies to the teeth, the narrower the focal trough in that region.

mcqs.q: If the patient's teeth are positioned TOO ANTERIOR (in front of the focal trough), the anterior teeth appear:
mcqs.explain: Teeth anterior to the focal trough are blurred and narrowed; teeth posterior to it are widened/elongated horizontally.

mcqs.q: If the teeth are positioned TOO POSTERIOR (behind the focal trough), they appear:
mcqs.explain: Structures behind the focal trough are magnified horizontally — they look elongated/wider.

mcqs.q: If the patient's chin is tipped DOWN too far, the occlusal plane shows an exaggerated:
mcqs.explain: Chin tipped down → an exaggerated 'smiling' curve; chin tipped up → a flat or reversed (frowning) occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: If the head is TURNED to one side, the teeth on that side appear:
mcqs.explain: When the head is turned, the teeth on the side toward which it is turned are reduced in size (narrowed).

mcqs.q: Digital panoramic images are commonly exported in which standard format?
mcqs.explain: DICOM is the standard for handling, storing, printing and transmitting medical images, including digital OPGs.

saqs.q: Define an OPG and the principle of tomography behind it.
saqs.a: OPG (OrthoPantomoGram) is a single tomographic image of both jaws and supporting structures. Tomography keeps one layer in focus while blurring other planes.

saqs.q: List three advantages and three disadvantages of panoramic radiography.
saqs.a: Advantages: whole dentition on one film, easy, quick, well-accepted. Disadvantages: poor detail/sharpness, magnification, distortion, overlapping, ghost shadows.

saqs.q: Describe correct patient positioning for an OPG.
saqs.a: Remove metal objects; lead apron, no thyroid collar; mid-sagittal plane ⊥ floor, Frankfurt plane ∥ floor; central incisors edge-to-edge in the bite block; align light guides.

saqs.q: Explain the two-disk principle of panoramic imaging.
saqs.a: The tube (Disk 1) and receptor (Disk 2) rotate in opposite directions; slit collimators narrow the beam, and the synchronized motion keeps a narrow focal trough sharp; the rotation centre moves with the curved arch.

saqs.q: Define the focal trough and its three dimensions.
saqs.a: A 3-D horseshoe-shaped zone (image layer) in which structures are reasonably sharp. Dimensions: antero-posterior, bucco-lingual, vertical.

saqs.q: What happens when teeth are positioned too anterior vs too posterior to the focal trough?
saqs.a: Too anterior → anterior teeth blurred & narrowed. Too posterior → structures elongated/widened horizontally.

saqs.q: How do head-tipping errors appear on a panoramic radiograph?
saqs.a: Chin tipped down → exaggerated "smiling" occlusal plane. Chin tipped up → flat/reversed smile. Head turned → teeth smaller on the turned side.
